Summary: high-value fintech customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive chat + heavy embeddings for fraud models. Heavy focus on deterministic throughput and predictable tail latency under bursts.

requirements_summary: Workloads: low-latency chat (multi-turn), high-throughput embedding generation for batch fraud scoring, reranking during query-time. Latency SLOs: p50 30-60ms, p95 <200ms for 2k token context, p99 under negotiation. Throughput target: sustained 600 qps with burst capacity to 1800 qps for short windows. Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit economics predictable. Must support VPC/private control plane and audit logging. Autoscaling: require policy definitions for warm pools, scale-up fast (<60s to add capacity for hot shards), conservative scale-down (cooldown >=10m), queueing strategy to avoid head-of-line blocking.

autoscaling_notes:
Key asks from customer:
- Warm pool: maintain a configurable pool of hot GPUs (suggested 10% of reserved) to serve instant spikes.
- Scale-up policy: detect sustained queue length > N for 12s OR CPU/GPU load > 80% for 8s => add nodes, target add latency < 60s for new replicas.
- Scale-down: conservative to avoid oscillation; cooldown 10m after scale-up, min-replicas floor tied to reserved commit.
- Queueing: implement soft queue with backpressure + prioritized routing for high-value customers/requests; overflow routing to a cheaper model variant (fallback) when latency budget exceeded.
- Routing/fallback: prefer model variants with quantized weights for cost/fallover; require consistent inference semantics.
- Warm caches: prefix/KV warmers for multi-turn chat to avoid KV cache misses on scale events.
- Monitoring: need per-GPU and per-route SLA dashboards (p50/p95/p99, queue depth, scale events).
poc_findings:
POC observations:
- Cold-starts responsible for most p95 spikes during abrupt 3x bursts. Warm pool reduces p95 by ~40% in the tested scenario.
- Auto-scaler reacted but new replicas took ~90s to reach warm cache primed state; root cause: model init + KV priming step.
- Queueing allowed throughput smoothing but increased tail latency for some high-priority requests; need prioritized lanes.
- Networking: initial VPC peering added ~12ms hop latency; acceptable but documented.
- Action items: implement cache priming during scale-up path, expose warm-pool sizing recommendation, define fallback model variants and cost impact.
